answer: A sponsor carries 69% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the gale liability is written down in the orchard ledger at admission, the pearl audit publishes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must therefore place its own capital behind each extra identity it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 24 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
